_readme: Coverage map for arXiv:1902.08184v4 -- 'Stability conditions in families',
Bayer, Lahoz, Macri, Nuer, Perry, Stellari. Created for issue #87 under
epic #79 (stability-families).
THIS IS NOT A TRUST RECORD AND NOT A MINT SURFACE. It is a zero-claim map
of the paper's structure onto statuses. formalization.yaml's `source`
remains the Bridgeland 2007 record, and registry/bridgeland2007.json
remains the only mint surface; nothing in this file changes either, and
nothing in this file may be cited as theorem coverage. The only status
that ever counts as coverage is 'formalized', and every entry below is
'target'.
Validation: python scripts/check_coverage_map.py
Run it before and after every edit to this file. It fails on any status
outside the vocabulary, any non-target status without complete evidence,
and any corpus-derived identifier key.
Update ownership: the owner (Chris Dare) promotes statuses; agents may
propose a promotion only by PR carrying the evidence fields the validator
demands, and 'formalized' additionally requires explicit owner acceptance
recorded in the entry. Adding sections, fixing titles against the pinned
PDF, and adding tracking links are ordinary edits; status promotion is
not.
Quotes: none are minted here. When a quote is later needed it must be
checked directly against the v4 artifact identified in `source` -- never
against the arXMCP corpus, whose rows carry no arXiv version (see
`corpus_note`).

near_term_coordinates.note: Weak stability conditions and HRS tilting. The repository holds abstract HRS-tilt machinery (Tilting/HeartTorsionPair.lean, reviewed under #86 with agreement theorems from #94), but that machinery binds to NO statement of this paper and its review explicitly disclaimed any such connection. Promotion past 'target' starts from a specific v4 statement, not from the existence of related machinery. PROMOTED target -> mapped 2026-08-08 with the #109 landing: slicingTorsionPair and its heart identification are the named candidates for display (14.1), with the slope-phase translation recorded as the open gap in the evidence. Definitions 14.1-14.3 candidates (#107), the Def 14.6 chain layer (#108), and the phase-language TiltingProperty candidate for Definition 14.12 (#110) are named in their COUNT UPDATE entries; they remain part of this same mapped hypothesis, not separate claims. UPDATE 2026-08-09: TiltSemistable.lean proves both directions of the phase-language semistable classification corresponding to Lemma 14.17 and its positive-imaginary/stable Hom-vanishing refinement, using the canonical original-cohomology sequence and tilted-heart images. TiltNoetherian.lean constructs the zero-charge torsion pair and noetherian data from the relative tilted-chain condition and also assembles it from phase-compatible envelopes. HarderNarasimhan.lean supplies the generic rank-decreasing quotient recursion; Support.lean proves support-property transport. UPDATE 2026-08-10: HeartCohomologySequence.lean identifies quotients of pure shifted objects by original torsion subobjects; TiltNoetherian.lean uses this bridge to saturate boundary-phase factors without a last-factor right-orthogonality premise; TiltHarderNarasimhan.lean iterates the reduction through both original H-minus-one and H-zero HN filtrations; and TiltAssembly.lean packages HN, noetherian, and support obligations from phase-compatible envelopes without an external rank or quotient-induction premise. A later 2026-08-10 landing derives the required shifted phase-compatible decompositions directly from the raw Definition 14.12 envelope clause: Ext-vanishing factors tilted zero-charge subobjects through the raw zero-charge quotient, the original noetherian condition terminates the resulting pullback chain, and maximal subobjects feed the HN/noetherian assembly. TiltAssembly.lean now packages all three heart-level obligations directly from TiltingProperty. A final 2026-08-10 landing proves the normalized weak slope--phase charge-ray identity in ChargeRay.lean, transports it through arbitrary integer shifts, and packages the phase-language weak upper tilt as a new WeakPreStabilityCondition in TiltPreStability.lean without an external compatibility premise. UPDATE 2026-08-11: SourceSlope.lean formalizes the finite slope cutoff, muPlus/muMinus endpoint comparison, the exact display (14.1) torsion pair, and the tilted-heart description. Tilting/Source proves the analytic identity between division by i-beta and positive rescaling of the phase rotation, constructs the exact charge Z/(i-beta), states a sign-separated Lemma 14.17 candidate and stable refinement, and packages Proposition 14.16's weak-prestability, support, and noetherian zero-charge conclusions as sourceTiltConclusion. The type-two candidate still stores phaseFree and the positive-imaginary Hom implication; the dated adversarial review must decide whether these are automatic from the printed v4 hypotheses. The coordinate stays mapped and requires owner signoff before any reviewed/formalized promotion.

SourceSlope.lean now formalizes the finite weak-slope to normalized-phase map, identifies muPlus/muMinus with the slicing endpoints, proves the two source inequalities equivalent to the phase bounds, and exposes slopeTorsionPair with slopeTilt_heart_iff. Tilting/Source further constructs Z/(i-beta), Proposition 14.16's conclusion package, and the exact sign-separated Lemma 14.17 statement. The mapped status records candidate bindings only; it is not a reviewed coverage claim.

near_term_coordinates.note: Uniform quadratic support across a family. PROMOTED target -> mapped 2026-08-11: Support/Quadratic.lean supplies a genuine bundled QuadraticForm and its implication to the norm support predicate; Support/Uniform.lean forces one form across an indexed family and supplies constant-family, reindexing, union-locus, and linear-equivalence transport; Support/ZeroChargeLattice.lean constructs the saturated subgroup generated by zero classes and proves its finite quotient free abelian; Support/Quotient.lean puts the descended charge and one uniform form on the real quotient; Weak/Support/Quadratic.lean binds these predicates to actual nonzero weak-semistable heart classes and stores charge compatibility. This is a numerical candidate mapping only. The indexed weak adapter currently uses one abstract category and heart, not varying geometric fibers; it does not define HN structures, boundedness/moduli functors, or the scalar-extension comparison from the integral quotient lattice to the real quotient space. Those are explicit boundaries, so the coordinate is not reviewed or formalized.

evidence.v4_check: Read directly from the pinned v4 PDF on 2026-08-11. Page 87: Definition 18.5 fixes a Mukai homomorphism and says a (weak) HN structure satisfies support with respect to a quadratic form Q when its torsion-heart stability data does; Lemma 18.6 identifies this with the same Q on every fiber. Page 101: Definition 21.9 forms the saturated zero-class subgroup Lambda_0 and the free quotient Lambda/Lambda_0. Page 102: Definition 21.15(4) places Q on the real quotient, requires negativity on the descended kernel and nonnegativity on every fiber semistable class; clause (5) is boundedness and remains outside this mapping.

near_term_coordinates.note: TARGET UPDATED 2026-08-11: Families/Basic.lean isolates candidate interfaces for universally locally constant charge, universal openness, weak generic openness, ordinary and weak HN integration after caller-designated Dedekind base changes, and boundedness. Families/Ordinary.lean combines Definition 20.5(1)-(3) with Definition 21.15(4)-(5), using the genuine quotient-uniform support predicate, and supplies a fully inhabited PUnit constant-family witness. Families/Weak.lean binds clause (0), charges, semistability loci, and quotient support to actual indexed weak stability functions on one fixed category and heart, again with an inhabited PUnit witness. Families/Theorem22.lean records the four source clauses used by Theorem 22.2 and every currently missing geometric dependency. Candidate declaration/source-coordinate links now exist, but governance keeps this coordinate at target pending adversarial review and owner acceptance; a later mapped status would still be only a candidate mapping, not a source-faithfulness verdict. The repository still has no schemes, varying fiber categories, base-change functors, relative hearts, moduli spaces, bounded-family constructions, complex-manifold structures, proof of Theorem 22.2, or implementation of the later Section 23 results.
